title: Sidecarless envelope encryption rotation + Terraform v2 upgrade roadmap (v0.1 draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches a proposed approach for: (1) moving our private deployment default from a sidecar-proxy envelope flow to a sidecarless envelope flow (client-side partial unwrap + quorum unwrap), and (2) coordinate a Terraform module v2 upgrade to support the new primitives, offline key ceremony automation, and immutable audit shipping for air-gapped customers.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Design a sidecarless envelope encryption pattern that reduces per-pod memory/CPU overhead and simplifies lifecycle for host-based services.
- Introduce a terraform module v2 (redwood/encryption-module) that exposes: keyset resource, key-version lifecycle (rotate/promote), remote-witness audit toggle, HSM-backed KEK binding, and split-keystore quorum unwrap configuration.
- Migration will be staged: opt-in per-cluster -> canary clusters -> bulk migration with automatic rollback hooks.
- Audit logs must be append-only, signed, and optionally replicated to a remote witness for air-gapped customers via signed, incremental bundles.

Background / motivation:
Current sidecar model: every pod has an encryption sidecar that holds a wrapping key for envelope encryption. Sidecars simplify rotation but add resource overhead, complicated DNS/redirect logic, and make node bootstrapping more brittle in air-gapped installs.
Problems we've seen:
- Sidecars double container counts and complicate OOM events for memory-constrained edge nodes.
- Terraform modules today assume inline sidecar resources and don't model split-keystore unwrap primitives.
- Audit requirements from a subset of regulated customers: immutable audit artifacts, key ceremony proof, and offline witness attestation for rotations.

Goals for this design:
1) Reduce runtime overhead for customer workloads by eliminating per-pod sidecars while preserving security guarantees.
2) Provide Terraform primitives for declarative key lifecycle management and offline rotations.
3) Ensure auditable, verifiable rotation and unwrap events even in air-gapped topologies.
4) Provide rollback-safe migration steps and a test harness for customers.

Design: Sidecarless envelope flow (high-level):
- Producer (application) performs envelope encryption using a short-lived CEK (content encryption key) generated locally.
- CEK is wrapped with a KEK that is not stored locally; instead applications call a lightweight KMS client library that provides an unwrap quorum API:
  - client sends wrapped CEK to 2-of-3 unwrappers (mix of HSMs and software KMS endpoints) as configured by Terraform resources.
  - Each unwrapper returns partial decryption shares which the client recombines to recover CEK.
  - For performance, implement a small local cache for CEKs with strict TTL and pinned to process lifecycle.
- For read-heavy services, provide a cache/forwarding option (service-level agent) that is cluster-scoped (single instance) instead of per-pod sidecars.

Key components and Terraform primitives required (module v2 sketch):
- resource "redwood_kms_keyset": manages key metadata (algorithm, length, HSM_binding boolean, rotation schedule).
- resource "redwood_kms_key_version": logical versions with lifecycle states (pending, active, retired, archived).
- resource "redwood_kms_unwrap_quorum": configuration that defines participants (list of endpoints), threshold (e.g., 2 of 3), transport settings (mTLS cert references).
- data "redwood_audit_witness": optional remote witness endpoint (for air-gapped, will be a bundle upload target).
- output: signed_rotation_manifest (url/hash) emitted after successful rotation plan apply.

Terraform upgrade notes (practical):
- v2 module will be backward compatible for existing keysets if the customer opts into "sidecarless = false". Default for new installs should be sidecarless = true.
- Migration plan requires a two-step terraform apply:
  1) Module v2 introduces a transitional resource redwood_kms_key_shadow which mirrors state for existing sidecar keys.
  2) A follow-up apply runs a rotation to generate keystore shares bound to the unwrap_quorum.
- Add acceptance tests: terraform apply --target=module.encryption["canary-cluster"] with mocked HSM endpoints (softHSM + local signer)
- Ensure state locking and explicit apply-time confirmation for rotation-sensitive changes (safeguard flag: rotate_confirm = true).

Rotation / key ceremony automation:
- Provide a CLI helper: rw-rotate --plan --sign-off that will:
  - generate rotation manifest (including non-sensitive metadata),
  - upload signed manifest to audit_witness (if configured),
  - trigger key version promotion across quorum endpoints via Terraform remote-exec hooks or API calls.
- Offline key ceremony mode: produce a signed bundle (JSON + signatures) that an operator can physically transfer to witness or air-gapped HSM admin. Bundle format: manifest.json, signatures/{participant}.sig, proof.bundle (SHA256).

Audit & observability:
- Audit events to capture: rotation_initiated, rotation_prepared, rotation_committed, unwrap_attempt, unwrap_success, unwrap_failure, key_revoked.
- Events must be signed by the involved participants and recorded as append-only records in the local audit log.
- For air-gapped setups: produce incremental signed bundles that a remote witness (or secure offline store) will ingest. Include a bundle index with monotonically increasing sequence numbers and hashes.
- Expose a terraform data source redwood_audit_manifest to allow other infra modules to fetch manifest metadata for compliance packaging.

Migration plan (staged):
1) Canary (opt-in): pick 2 internal clusters, enable sidecarless and key_shadow resources. Run smoke tests, latency checks, and functional unwrap tests.
2) Customer opt-in: allow customers to enable sidecarless in their module configuration (toggle). Provide a migration checklist script.
3) Bulk migration: schedule maintenance windows, set rotate_confirm=true, run rw-rotate --plan and --apply. Monitor unwrap_failure_rate metric and automatic rollback threshold (if unwrap_failure_rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes, trigger rollback).
4) Post-migration: retire old sidecar KEKs after 30 days of stable metrics. Archive old key versions with signed manifest attached.

Testing / harness:
- Create a test harness repository infra/encryption-e2e that uses:
  - softHSM + PKCS11 emulators,
  - a quorum of 3 endpoints (two software, one HSM-emulated),
  - synthetic workloads for unwrap latency under concurrent loads.
- Add chaos tests: drop one unwrapper mid-unwrap, saturate network between client and quorum.
- Add compatibility tests with existing sidecar flow to ensure rollback path works.

Security considerations / threat model notes:
- Quorum unwrap reduces single-host compromise risk but requires careful protection of transport keys (mTLS identities) and host attestation.
- Supply-chain: rotation manifests must be signed by an offline key stored in HSM; Terraform state must never contain plaintext key material.
- Replays: signed sequence numbers and the bundle hash chain protect against replayed rotations.
- Failure modes: network partitions during rotation — mitigation: do not promote new active key until N of quorum endpoints confirm commit; provide explicit operator override with multi-signer confirmation.

Operational runbook (short):
- Pre-checks: run ./scripts/check-prereqs.sh (ensures HSM endpoints responsive, CA certs present, terraform version >= 1.5).
- Dry-run: rw-rotate --plan -> review signed_rotation_manifest.json -> push to audit witness (dry).
- Apply: rw-rotate --apply (observability hook will stream events to Console).
- Post-checks: verify unwrap_success_rate > 99.9% and latency P95 within 2x baseline.

Open questions / unresolved items (TODO):
- Decide default CEK cache TTL (30s ? 2m?). Tradeoff: latency vs exposure.
- Operator UX: do we provide a lightweight cluster-scoped agent for read-heavy services or rely solely on client libs? (Linked PR explores both: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412)
- Air-gapped witness ingestion tooling: should the witness be a small stateless HTTP ingest or a signed-bundle-only ingest?
- Legal/Compliance: what retention windows for archived key manifests satisfy SOC2 / GDPR requests?

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: prototype client unwrap library (deadline 2025-02-28).
- Marco: terraform module v2 skeleton + transitional shadow resource (PR by 2025-03-10).
- Lina: test harness with softHSM scenario + chaos tests (ETA 2025-03-20).
- Product (Priya): collect two early-adopter customers for canary program (by 2025-02-20).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working sketch. Focus feedback on the migration safety model and audit chain format. The intent is to reduce runtime complexity for customers while preserving strong rotation guarantees and an auditable trail suitable for regulated workloads.

References / links:
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412
- RFC draft (internal): confluence.redwood.internal/r/encryption-sidecarless-rfc (WIP)
- Jira: JIRA-RDW-1324 (encryption module v2), JIRA-INF-2048 (quorum unwrap feature)

Quick checklist (for next meeting):

- [ ] Approve terraform transitional resource design
